clue.text: Recently stolen items, things of outstanding interest

definitions.meaning: first meaning: slang for freshly stolen goods, still 'hot'
second meaning: something exciting or highly impressive

explanation.walkthrough: The comma makes it read like a description of a museum's newest exhibits; it is two separate senses of one phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: Stolen goods are called 'hot' while police still look for them, and the same phrase is idiomatic praise for anything exciting.

clue.text: Stature of hard rowing crew

parts.note: H is the pencil-grade abbreviation for hard
an eight is a racing boat crewed by eight rowers

explanation.surface: A rowing crew is admired for how tall and powerful its members are.
explanation.definitionFit: Stature is a synonym for how tall a person stands.

clue.text: Contemptible person with small weapon, a jack-o'-lantern?

parts.note: a toad is a loathsome, despicable person
S is the clothing-size abbreviation for small
tool is slang for a gun or weapon

explanation.surface: A nasty character carrying a little weapon is likened to a Halloween pumpkin.
explanation.walkthrough: The jack-o'-lantern here is not the carved pumpkin but a glowing orange mushroom of that name; the question mark marks the definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: The jack-o'-lantern is a poisonous orange fungus, so it is one example of the umbrella-shaped growth named here.

clue.text: Poet's new titles describing love

indicators.note: to describe can mean to draw a line around, so these letters enclose the next piece
making something new reworks it, so these letters take a fresh order

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged
love is zero in tennis, shaped like O

explanation.surface: A poet's latest book titles all revolve around love.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is', joining the poet to the wordplay. The shuffled TITLES go around O, which sits before the final T.
explanation.definitionFit: T. S. Eliot wrote The Waste Land and is among the best-known modern poets.

clue.text: All over the farm, food, too contaminated

indicators.note: something contaminated has been spoiled and altered, so these letters are jumbled

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A contamination scare spreads across the whole farm and its food as well.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means covering the entire body, hence everywhere or completely.

clue.text: Turning point in cold river, the Thames at Oxford

parts.note: C marks the cold tap
R is a standard abbreviation for river
the stretch of the Thames flowing through Oxford is traditionally called the Isis

explanation.surface: Something momentous happens on a cold river, the Thames where it passes Oxford.
explanation.walkthrough: The Isis is the local name for the Thames around Oxford, familiar from university rowing.
explanation.definitionFit: A crisis is the decisive moment when events take a turn, originally the turning point of an illness.

clue.text: A German schoolmaster served up an Italian dish

indicators.note: in a down entry, going up means the letters read from bottom to top

parts.note: Otto is a typical German man's name
pupils address a male teacher as Sir

explanation.surface: A German teacher dishes up an Italian meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Served up' looks like cooking but asks for the whole of OTTO SIR to be read upward in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Risotto is the rice dish from northern Italy cooked slowly in stock.

clue.text: Smart wife is employed by southern hospital

indicators.note: someone employed by a firm is taken inside it, so these letters sit within the next pair

parts.note: S abbreviates southern
H is the map-sign abbreviation for hospital
W is the genealogical abbreviation for wife
taken as written

explanation.surface: A well-dressed wife works at a hospital in the south.
explanation.definitionFit: Swish is informal for fashionable and expensive-looking, a synonym of smart.

clue.text: Support a coercive measure

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to approve or authorise
second meaning: a penalty imposed on a country to force compliance

explanation.walkthrough: The word is famous for meaning both itself and its near opposite: official approval and an official penalty.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means give official approval; as a noun it means a penalty such as a trade embargo.

clue.text: Boss put career in jeopardy, accepting ring as bribe

indicators.note: accepting means taking something in, so another letter joins this collection
something in jeopardy is at risk of being thrown into disorder, so the letters are scrambled

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged
a ring is round, like the letter O

explanation.surface: A boss risks a career by taking a ring offered as a bribe.
explanation.walkthrough: Cerberus is the three-headed dog guarding the classical underworld; travellers threw it a honey cake to pass, hence the phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: A sop to Cerberus is a gift made to placate a troublesome guardian or official, in effect a bribe.

clue.text: Furious, corsair losing face

indicators.note: the face is the front, so losing it drops the opening letter

parts.note: a corsair is a pirate, especially of the Barbary coast

explanation.surface: A pirate is enraged at being humiliated.
explanation.definitionFit: Irate is a synonym for very angry.

clue.text: Ruling passion of old boy at meeting

indicators.note: being at something places one beside it, so the two parts sit side by side

parts.note: OB abbreviates old boy, a former pupil
a session is a meeting of a council or court

explanation.surface: A former pupil's consuming enthusiasm shows at a reunion.
explanation.definitionFit: An obsession is a fixation that dominates the mind, a passion that rules one's thoughts.

clue.text: Keeps that man's heroin and cannabis

parts.note: to keep something is to have it
the possessive of he
H is slang for heroin

explanation.surface: A man is caught holding two illegal drugs.
explanation.definitionFit: Hashish is resin from the cannabis plant, smoked as a drug.

clue.text: Pop has injection after 12

indicators.note: following something means coming behind it, so this piece goes second

parts.note: the answer to 12 is a drug, and pot is slang for it
a shot is an injection, as of vaccine

explanation.surface: Father gets a jab following his drug use.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pop' poses as Dad but is the verb sense of taking a quick shot at something.
explanation.definitionFit: A pot shot is a casual, quickly aimed shot, and to have a pop at something is the same idea.

clue.text: Loaded with gold, both row boat out

indicators.note: out suggests something put out of order or out of place, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: W is short for with
or is gold in heraldry
the letters taken as written

explanation.surface: Two people laden with gold row out in a boat.
explanation.walkthrough: A bob is an old British shilling coin; the phrase is a jokey understatement for being rich.
explanation.definitionFit: Loaded is slang for rich, and being worth a bob or two is a British idiom for having plenty of money.

clue.text: Money girl needed for an old car

parts.note: tin is old slang for money
a girl's name, short for Elizabeth

explanation.surface: A girl needs cash to buy a vintage car.
explanation.definitionFit: Tin Lizzie was the nickname of the Ford Model T, an early mass-produced motor car.

clue.text: Range of toasted crumpets

indicators.note: toasting changes food's form, so these letters are cooked into a new order

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A selection of crumpets, all toasted.
explanation.walkthrough: Crumpets are spongy griddle cakes eaten toasted with butter in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: A spectrum is a full range or scale, as in the political spectrum.

clue.text: To add to distress of platoon, hygiene is badly affected

indicators.note: something badly affected is damaged and disordered, so the letters are scrambled

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A soldiers' unit suffers further misery when its cleanliness slips.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to make a painful situation worse or to exaggerate suffering.

clue.text: Greek character, moronic criminal

indicators.note: criminal suggests something crooked or bent out of shape, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A dim-witted Greek crook.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Character' suggests a person to fit 'moronic criminal', but it means a letter of the alphabet.
explanation.definitionFit: Omicron is the fifteenth letter of the Greek alphabet.

clue.text: Good writer of thrillers is better

parts.note: G abbreviates good
Eric Ambler was a British author of spy thrillers

explanation.surface: A good thriller writer is judged superior.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Better' reads as an adjective but is a noun: one who bets.
explanation.definitionFit: A better is someone who bets, the same as one who gambles.

clue.text: Closed trunk as well

parts.note: a door pushed to is closed
the boot is the British name for a car's trunk

explanation.surface: A trunk is shut too.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom to boot means in addition or besides.

clue.text: Capital Jack provided, got by force?

parts.note: a jack is a playing card
provided means on condition that
F is the physics symbol for force

explanation.surface: A city captured by force, if Jack had his way.
explanation.definitionFit: Cardiff is the capital city of Wales.

clue.text: Sticky substance found in hare's innards

indicators.note: something found in a phrase sits inside it, ready to be picked out

parts.note: the letters run across the two words

explanation.surface: Something gooey is discovered inside a hare.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Innards' adds to the anatomy picture while also pointing inside the words.
explanation.definitionFit: Resin is the gummy substance exuded by trees such as pines.

clue.text: Almost prevent Dr No seizing one young child

indicators.note: seizing means grabbing and holding, so these letters close around another
almost means not quite all, so the last letter is cut

parts.note: to ban is to prohibit
MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a doctor's qualification
taken as written
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone nearly stops the Bond villain Dr No grabbing a child.
explanation.walkthrough: Dr No looks like the Bond villain, but Dr and No are separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Bambino is the Italian word for a baby or small child, used informally in English.

clue.text: River rose unexpectedly, forming a lake

indicators.note: happening unexpectedly means not in the usual order, so the letters come out rearranged

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A river flooded without warning and made a lake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rose' reads as the river rising, not a flower.
explanation.definitionFit: A reservoir is an artificial lake built to store water.

clue.text: Left A-Z on one round Italian region

parts.note: L abbreviates left
taken as written, the letters of the street atlas name
I is the Roman numeral one
a round shape like the letter O

explanation.surface: Someone abandoned their road atlas on a tour of an Italian region.
explanation.walkthrough: An A-Z is a British street-map book of a city.
explanation.definitionFit: Lazio is the region of central Italy containing Rome.

clue.text: Mother meeting grandmother tomorrow

indicators.note: meeting means coming up against, so the two parts are placed side by side

parts.note: Ma is an informal word for mother
Nana is a familiar name for a grandmother

explanation.surface: Mum is visiting Granny the next day.
explanation.definitionFit: Mañana is Spanish for tomorrow, used in English for putting things off.

clue.text: Hungry? Tureen is prepared

indicators.note: prepared food has been made up from raw ingredients, so these letters are reworked

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A host asks if you are peckish, since the soup is ready.
explanation.definitionFit: Esurient is a literary adjective meaning greedy or famished.
